title: Tribe structure, size and St. Joseph's Night
summary: Cahn describes tribes of 12-15 men with spy boy, flag boy and chiefs, and parades on Mardi Gras Day and St. Joseph's Night.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: The Mardi Gras Indians are groups. I think there are approximately 12 tribes in the city, and each tribe is pretty well defined with approximately 12 to 15 men. There is a spy boy, the flag boy, the first chief, the chief, the assistant chief, and as other people come in, they will find a place for them. But it usually limits itself to about right between 12 and 15, and they come out on Mardi Gras Day. And historically, it's much more visual, I think, than audio, because they have these exotic costumes that they make themselves, and historically they only use them twice a year. Mardi Gras Day and St. Joseph's Night. Up until now, I've not been able to really find out why they picked St. Joseph's Night, except that, as the people would say in olden times, it's the only holiday between Mardi Gras and Easter. So, being the only holiday, and strangely enough, a large segment of the Indians are Catholic, and they do pick St. Joseph's Night, and that's the only reason I can come up with that they pick that to have their Indian dance, and they parade on the streets through the various parts of the neighborhood on St. Joseph's Night.
Now, how many people make up these Mardi Gras groups? I mean, make up the Indian groups?
In one tribe. And there are about that many tribes, 12 to 15, or maybe more.
